data.note:
Note: Specimen s_d4cbe87ca5 unblinded as lactacystin (PubChem CID 6610292, e16, ChEMBL CHEMBL374308 with no curated mechanism in ChEMBL but BBBC021 annotates Protein degradation). Literature confirms lactacystin is a classic 20S proteasome inhibitor (e.g., PMID:18650992, PMID:39988264, PMID:17880361 describe "proteasome inhibitor lactacystin").

My blinded conclusion DNA replication (p=0.82) was incorrect per code. I followed the NSC vote 4/4 DNA replication with high cosine similarity 0.76-0.90 to methotrexate/floxuridine/mitoxantrone (e6) and the monotonic dose-response: 0.3 µM DNA mean +5.36z / integrated +4.43z then 1→10 µM progressive loss to -8.45z/-6.78z with cell_area +6.8z and cell_nuc_ratio +9.25z (e2,e3,e7,e9). I interpreted this as replication stress with cell enlargement and under-replication at high dose, discounting Protein degradation because the atlas had no Protein degradation neighbors in top 10 and no NSC votes.

Reflection: Protein degradation is sparsely represented in the reference atlas (leave-one-compound-out excluded lactacystin itself), so NSC defaulted to the nearest abundant class - DNA replication (5/10 neighbors, Kinase inhibitors 4/10, e6). Proteasome inhibition produces overlapping morphology: G1/S arrest, cell enlargement, reduced proliferation (cell_count -3.6z) and at cytotoxic doses apoptotic DNA loss/fragmentation mimicking reduced integrated DNA, which my 0.3-10 µM window captured as a biphasic DNA shift without low-dose proteotoxic signature or ubiquitin/aggresome readout. With only 4 wells I did not sample 0.003-0.1 µM to resolve early accumulation of cyclins/p21 expected for proteasome block, nor did I have a proteasome-specific feature (e.g., ubiquitin foci, tubulin unchanged e12, mitotic-like down e10 already argued against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule). A follow-up EdU/PI cell-cycle + p21/ubiquitin staining would have discriminated DNA replication block from proteasomal G1 arrest despite atlas similarity.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is lactacystin (PubChem CID 6610292) - truth MoA Protein degradation. My submitted conclusion was DNA replication p=0.82 - verdict incorrect. Review approved the call as favored at the time, but approval does not change outcome.

What the evidence got right:

At 0.3-10 uM (doses 4-7, rep 1 only) there was a coherent dose-dependent phenotype: nuc_dna_mean z +5.4 at 0.3 uM (e3) -> -2.7 to -5.2 at 1-3 uM (implied by e7/e9 trends) -> -8.4 at 10 uM (e2), nuc_dna_integrated rho=-1.00 (e9), cell_nuc_area_ratio rho=+1.00 (e8) with z +4.2 at 1 uM (e5), +5.7 at 3 uM (e4), +9.3 at 10 uM (e2), plus cell_area/cell_major_axis enlargement (e2,e4,e5) and decreasing frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.95 (e10). Against mitotic/microtubule classes that was correct: tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e12) is non-significant and frac_mitotic_like fell, consistent with no mitotic arrest. That discrimination held.

What misled me and why:

1. Atlas reliance without a Protein degradation option. compare_to_reference_atlas (e6) returned NSC vote 4/4 DNA replication and k-neighbors DNA replication 5/10, Kinase inhibitors 4/10, Microtubule destabilizers 1/10. No Protein degradation class appeared in the neighbor list. I treated 4/4 NSC as strong support for DNA replication and discounted Kinase inhibitors because mean similarity ~0.55 vs 0.70 for DNA replication in review, but I did not account for atlas under-representation of proteasome inhibition in this cell-line/timepoint. The hypothesis set I updated (e13) did not even contain Protein degradation: DNA replication 0.82, Kinase inhibitors 0.08, DNA damage 0.05, Protein synthesis 0.03. Protein synthesis 0.03 was the closest proteostasis category and I gave it near-zero weight because e6 contradicted it.

2. Phenotypic overlap misinterpreted as replication stress. The biphasic to monotonic flip in DNA content (+5.4 at 0.3 uM to -8.4 at 10 uM) and cell enlargement with cell_nuc_area_ratio increase (e2,e4,e5,e7,e8,e9) was read as S-phase block/replication stress. Lactacystin is a 20S proteasome inhibitor PMID 18650992 PMID 39988264 PMID 17880361 PMID 17561309 PMID 21377449 - proteasome inhibition also arrests cell cycle, can produce increased then decreased DNA intensity and cell enlargement due to failed degradation of cyclins/cell-cycle regulators and general proteotoxicity, and loss of mitotic figures (e10). Without a proteasome-specific readout (ubiquitin accumulation, proteasome activity, p21/cyclin levels) the imaging features are not discriminative between these MoAs in this atlas.

3. Acquisition choices amplified the error. I acquired only 4 wells, all single replicates at the high end (doses 4-7 rep1), leaving 4 of 8 doses unused (e1) and no sampling of 0.003-0.1 uM or rep2. Dose-response correlations of rho= +/-1.00 p=0 (e7,e8,e9) with n=4 monotonic points looked decisive but with one replicate per dose they are fragile and cannot establish replication specificity. Cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e11) showed only moderate cytotoxicity, so I inferred cytostatic replication block rather than considering proteasome inhibition can be cytostatic with similar cell-count profile at these doses.

I did not miss a low-dose differential signal - I never sampled it. Lookup after unblinding showed no curated ChEMBL mechanisms for lactacystin (e15/e16) but literature search for lactacystin proteasome inhibitor (e17/e18) aligns with the known MoA PMID 18650992 PMID 21377449. My next-experiment proposal (EdU/PI flow + phospho-H2AX) would not have resolved proteasome vs replication without a ubiquitin/proteasome assay.

Lesson: when NSC is unanimous but neighbor set lacks the true class, treat as atlas limitation, not confirmation; retain Protein degradation/proteasome hypothesis for compounds causing cell enlargement + DNA content shifts + mitotic loss, and budget low-dose replicates and orthogonal proteostasis readouts before assigning p=0.82.
